pr_body:
Enhacement: makes `Mesh::generate_triangle_mesh()` handle `PRIMITIVE_TRIANGLE_STRIP` (besides already supported `PRIMITIVE_TRIANGLES`).

Bugfix: now `Mesh::generate_triangle_mesh()` ignores surfaces with incorrect vertex/index count and shows an error for each such surface. Previously it was checking only the total amount of vertices/indices (sum of counts) so for example it wouldn't error out when having 2 surfaces with 1 and 2 vertices respectively, it would incorrectly deduce it's 1 triangle (1+2=3 vertices/indices).

Fixes #61552.

issue_context.title: SurfaceTool triangle strips don't create faces in a Mesh
comments:
Looking through the code, it looks like it is designed to only work with primitive type ``Triangles``. That is not to say it can't work with other primitive types, but it won't be trivial to extend it.

Internally ``create_trimesh_collision()`` calls ``generate_triangle_mesh()`` which only works with triangles. One option is to convert the mesh to using the triangles primitve before generating the triangle mesh. Another option is to extend ``generate_triangle_mesh()`` to support other primitive types.

@clayjohn I'm already looking at this, specifically to make `generate_triangle_mesh()` support other primitive types (`PRIMITIVE_TRIANGLE_STRIP` in `3.x`/`master` plus `PRIMITIVE_TRIANGLE_FAN` in `3.x`).

review_comments: Is it possible for ``len`` to equal 1? If so, this will need to handle that case as well. could just change ``len == 0`` to ``len <= 1``

Not sure if I get what exactly you're asking about. Is 1 a valid `len`? I don't think so. 0 vertices/indexes is just an empty surface which I think is technically valid (hence it's handled without an error). Otherwise it needs at least 3 vertices/indexes, 1 is not enough to form the first triangle. And currently such case (1 vertex/index) is handled, it will result in an error (hence `faces_size += ...` line will not be executed in such case).
There's an err check on the previous line that indeed ensures it won't be < 3.
Ah right ERR_CONTINUE_MSG continues the for loop. It doesn't just "continue" on to the next line.
